answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, so influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster joined to honest participants by a sparse external cut has low conductance; min-cut transitivity bounds how much voting weight can cross that boundary, limiting its aggregate influence. Like a jetty resisting a spiral tide against basalt, the boundary impedes—but does not eliminate—fabricated trust.
